CREATE TABLE categories (
  category_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  category_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,

  description TEXT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(40),
  country VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  city VARCHAR(100),
  customer_segment VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL  -- Either individual or business. Business customers may have a credit_limit.,
  credit_limit NUMERIC(12,2)  -- Maximum outstanding balance allowed. NULL for individual customers.,
  signup_date DATE NOT NULL,
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE departments (
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,

  last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(40),
  hire_date DATE NOT NULL,
  job_title VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  salary NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  manager_id INTEGER  -- This employee's manager, NULL for the top of the org chart.,
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE inventory (
  inventory_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,

  reorder_level INTEGER NOT NULL  -- Stock threshold below which the product should be reordered.,

);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Price charged at the time of sale, not the product's current list price.,
  discount_pct NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL  -- Percentage discount, 0-100. Line revenue is quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100).
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  employee_id INTEGER  -- Sales representative handling the order. NULL for self-service online orders.,
  order_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  required_date DATE,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  total_amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Denormalised order total including shipping. Should equal the sum of its order_items after discount, plus shipping_cost.,
  shipping_cost NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE payments (
  payment_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payment_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  payment_method VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  transaction_ref VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_name VARCHAR(250) NOT NULL,
  sku VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  category_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  supplier_id INTEGER,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Current list price. Historical sale prices live on order_items.unit_price.,
  unit_cost NUMERIC(12,2)  -- Cost to acquire the product. Revenue minus cost gives margin.,
  weight_kg NUMERIC(10,3),
  is_discontinued BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE shipments (
  shipment_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  shipped_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
  delivered_date TIMESTAMPTZ  -- When the shipment reached the customer. NULL if not yet delivered.,
  carrier VARCHAR(100),
  tracking_number VARCHAR(100),
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL
);

  supplier_name VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
  contact_name VARCHAR(150),
  contact_email VARCHAR(255),
  phone VARCHAR(40),
  country VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  city VARCHAR(100),
  rating NUMERIC(3,2),
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  warehouse_name VARCHAR(150) NOT NULL,
  country VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  city VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  capacity_units INTEGER NOT NULL,
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL

Question: List customers whose orders span over 10 product categories.

PostgreSQL query: /no_think

SELECT c.customer_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) AS category_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT p.category_id) > 10 ORDER BY category_count DESC

SELECT p.product_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_pct / 100)) AS revenue FROM products p JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 50

);

  signup_date DATE NOT NULL,
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE departments (
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  department_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  location VARCHAR(150),
  annual_budget NUMERIC(14,2),
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(40),
  hire_date DATE NOT NULL,
  job_title VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  salary NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  manager_id INTEGER  -- This employee's manager, NULL for the top of the org chart.,
  is_active BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE inventory (
  inventory_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity_on_hand INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reorder_level INTEGER NOT NULL  -- Stock threshold below which the product should be reordered.,
  last_restocked_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE order_items (
  order_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Price charged at the time of sale, not the product's current list price.,
  discount_pct NUMERIC(5,2) NOT NULL  -- Percentage discount, 0-100. Line revenue is quantity * unit_price * (1 - discount_pct / 100).
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  employee_id INTEGER  -- Sales representative handling the order. NULL for self-service online orders.,
  order_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  required_date DATE,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  total_amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Denormalised order total including shipping. Should equal the sum of its order_items after discount, plus shipping_cost.,
  shipping_cost NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE payments (
  payment_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  payment_date TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  amount NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  payment_method VARCHAR(30) NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  transaction_ref VARCHAR(100)
);

CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_name VARCHAR(250) NOT NULL,
  sku VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
  category_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  supplier_id INTEGER,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Current list price. Historical sale prices live on order_items.unit_price.,
  unit_cost NUMERIC(12,2)  -- Cost to acquire the product. Revenue minus cost gives margin.,
  weight_kg NUMERIC(10,3),
  is_discontinued BOOLEAN NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

  shipment_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  shipped_date TIMESTAMPTZ,

WITH RECURSIVE tree AS ( SELECT category_id, category_name, parent_category_id, 0 AS depth FROM categories WHERE category_name = 'Books & Media' UNION ALL SELECT c.category_id, c.category_name, c.parent_category_id, t.depth + 1 FROM categories c JOIN tree t ON c.parent_category_id = t.category_id) SELECT category_id, category_name, depth FROM tree WHERE depth > 0 ORDER BY depth, category_name

SELECT s.supplier_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_pct / 100)) AS revenue FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 15

CREATE TABLE categories (

CREATE TABLE departments (
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  department_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  location VARCHAR(150),

);

  employee_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  first_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  last_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  email VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  phone VARCHAR(40),
  hire_date DATE NOT NULL,
  job_title VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
  salary NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL,
  department_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  manager_id INTEGER  -- This employee's manager, NULL for the top of the org chart.,

);

  inventory_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  warehouse_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity_on_hand INTEGER NOT NULL,
  reorder_level INTEGER NOT NULL  -- Stock threshold below which the product should be reordered.,

);

  order_item_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  quantity INTEGER NOT NULL,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Price charged at the time of sale, not the product's current list price.,

  order_id INTEGER NOT NULL,

);

CREATE TABLE products (
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
  product_name VARCHAR(250) NOT NULL,

  category_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  supplier_id INTEGER,
  unit_price NUMERIC(12,2) NOT NULL  -- Current list price. Historical sale prices live on order_items.unit_price.,
  unit_cost NUMERIC(12,2)  -- Cost to acquire the product. Revenue minus cost gives margin.,
  weight_kg NUMERIC(10,3),

  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
);

Question: List our 50 highest earning suppliers.

PostgreSQL query: /no_think

SELECT s.supplier_name, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price * (1 - oi.discount_pct / 100)) AS revenue FROM suppliers s JOIN products p ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY s.supplier_id, s.supplier_name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 50

SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.is_active = FALSE AND o.order_date > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00' - INTERVAL '2 months' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY last_order DESC

SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name, MAX(o.order_date) AS last_order FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.is_active = FALSE AND o.order_date > TIMESTAMPTZ '2026-08-01 00:00:00+00:00' - INTERVAL '5 months' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name ORDER BY last_order DESC
